newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's central bank cuts key interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Norway's central bank cuts key interest rates.

text.p: Norway's central bank said on Tuesday it was cutting its rate for overnight deposits, the credit rate, to 4.0 percent from 4.50 percent.
The overnight lending rate, charged to commercial and savings banks, was reduced to 6.0 percent from 6.50 percent.
Both measures will take effect on Wednesday.
Central Bank Governor Kjell Storvik said in a statement the decision came in response to recent developments in the money and foreign exchange.
The crown, which has appreciated strongly recently, stood at 101.17 crowns on the reverse ECU index at 1130 GMT.
"The crown exchange rate has been under persistent pressure and the Norwegian Bank has purchased considerable amounts of foreign currency to curb the rise in the crown exchange rate," Storvik said.

"A reduction in the Norwegian Bank's exchange rates now seemed appropriate to reduce the appreciation pressure," Storvik said. "In view of the strengthening of the crown exchange rate which has taken place, the interest rate reduction will not entail that monetary policy will have a more expansionary effect on the economy."
He also said that in Norway, where the primary objective of monetary policy is exchange rate stability, it is fiscal policy that must assume the main responsbility for stabilising the economy.

Given the bank's reluctance to trim interest rates and risk triggering inflation, this has meant increasingly selling crowns partly to keep a lid on the crown's rise and partly to cover investments for the government petroleum fund into which the country's swelling budget surplus will be invested.
The bank has sold more than 60 billion crowns so far this year compared with an estimated budget surplus for 1996 of 37.9 billion crowns.
The central bank recently told the government that a tight fiscal policy was necessary in 1997 and at least in line with the state budget proposal now being discussed in parliament.
On March 7 the central bank last trimmed both key rates by 0.25 percentage points, the first key interest rate cut since February 1994.
